reason:
Review escalation at round 3, cause hard-cap, so the only option is accept, and it is allowed only when the open
design-wrong findings are wrong or the fix in place already answers them. The round-3 fixer's text in the decision
record answers all three open keys:
- F1 (d12-non-exec-calls-outside-cell-model): D12 now treats a model call as one top-level rollout call item. It
  names the collaboration spawn_agent and send_message calls as function_call items and scopes the payload and
  latest-cell sentences to nested calls. A payload whose tool_name is neither Bash nor apply_patch gets no nudge
  and the rollout is left unread for it. A function_call ends a lookup_run or edit_run chain, and the acceptance
  criterion covers that case. I checked the cited 2026-11-15 rollout: it holds 21 custom_tool_call exec items and
  4 collaboration function_call items (2 spawn_agent, 2 send_message), as D12 now states. The skipped spike does
  not affect the design, because the rule holds whether or not the hook fires.
- F2 (d1-scan-reaches-probe-literals): D1 defines a launch-spec literal as a Spec literal that sets Prompt. D1's
  scan, D4's scan and the producer table skip the attach probes. A producer that fills its prompt inline gets its
  render split out, and the Notes match. I checked bouncer.go: the awaitLiveJudge and awaitLiveSeed literals set
  only OutputFiles, Role, Segment and Round, while runSeedSpawn and judgeCall set Prompt.
- F3 (mechanical): D12 resolves both paths against each call's CommandExecution cwd and applies the
  modification-time test. The spike rollout shows that cwd as a file:// URL and parsed_cmd paths as written.
I recorded the ruling as an arbiter decision so the plan writer reads these findings as answered, not as
unconverged gaps. Then I accepted round 3.
